transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I haven’t really been feeling like myself. It’s not that anything is terribly wrong on paper, you know? My wife tries to get us back into our old Sunday routines, things we used to enjoy, and even when something goes well at work… I just don’t really feel happy about it. Or close to her, the way I should.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been bothering me. I thought maybe I should talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I suppose… it’s been longer than I’d like to admit. Since that retrofit accident, really—about a year and seven months ago. I kept thinking it would sort of pass on its own, but it’s just… stayed around.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before the accident?

Not really… I mean, I still go along with things. My wife tries to get us doing our old Sunday routines, and I try to act like I’m enjoying it, because I don’t want to disappoint her. But the feeling just doesn’t really show up.

Even when something good happens at work, I know I should feel pleased, and I can say the right things, but inside it’s kind of flat. I don’t feel real happiness the way I used to… or that closeness with her. I’m not sure if that makes sense.
Have you had periods like this before the accident?

No… not really. I mean, I had normal ups and downs like anyone, but nothing that stuck around like this. This really seems to have started after the retrofit accident, about… a year and seven months ago. I kept hoping it would just settle down, but it hasn’t.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead since the accident?

I… no, I don’t think so. Not in the sense of wanting to hurt myself or making any kind of plan. I don’t want to worry anyone or make it sound more dramatic than it is. I’ve just felt… not myself, I guess. But no, I haven’t been looking to harm myself.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make a big thing out of it, but I guess I am on edge a lot.

At work, when I’m on the floor, I’m constantly checking things—gauges, exits, where people’s hands are, where the emergency stops are. I tell myself it’s just being careful, being responsible, you know? But it’s… probably more than most people are doing.

Even in meetings, I’ll pick a seat where I can see the door. It sounds a little excessive when I say it out loud, but it makes me feel like I can keep track of things. Is that the kind of worry you mean?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since the accident?
Not that I’ve really noticed, no. My clothes fit about the same, I think. I haven’t been tracking it closely or anything, but I don’t think there’s been a significant weight loss.
Do you feel like you're able to find some pleasure or interest in things for at least a few days a week?

I… I still do things, if that counts. Like my wife tries to get us back into our old Sunday routines, and I’ll go along with it. And if something goes well at work, I know I should feel good about it.

But honestly, I don’t really feel real happiness from it. Or closeness, even when she’s trying. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely shut down, but… the feeling just doesn’t seem to come the way it used to.
How many months have you been feeling this way without any significant improvement?

I guess… since the accident. The retrofit one.

It’s been about a year and seven months now, if I’m counting right. I kept thinking it would ease up with time, and maybe I’d just get back to normal, but… not much has really changed. Does that answer what you mean by “without improvement”?
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities and feelings of detachment from your wife are present every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still go through the motions, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just refusing everything or anything like that.

But the lack of real happiness, or feeling close to my wife… that’s pretty much there every day. Even when she’s trying to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routine, or something at work goes well, it just doesn’t really land the way it should. Is that what you mean?
Have you had other periods in your life where you felt this way before the accident?

No… not like this. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches like anyone, but this specific feeling — the distance, the lack of real enjoyment — that’s really been since the retrofit accident.

So… about a year and seven months now. I don’t want to overstate it, but I can’t honestly say I remember being this way before that.
Do you feel like your symptoms have been consistently worse over the past two weeks?

I’m not sure I’d say “consistently worse,” exactly. The last couple weeks have felt… pretty much like the same bad pattern, if that makes sense.

Maybe some days stand out more than others, but I haven’t really noticed a clear shift where I’d say, “yes, it’s definitely gotten worse.” Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Has your current period of feeling this way lasted for more than two years?

No… not more than two years. It’s been a long time, but if I’m being accurate, it started after the retrofit accident, so about a year and seven months ago.

That’s still a while, obviously, but not past two years. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you felt normal and your symptoms improved significantly since the accident?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, there have been better days here and there, sure, but not a stretch of two months where I felt like myself again.

It’s more like this has just been going on since the retrofit accident — about a year and seven months now. I wish I could say there was a real break in it, but I don’t think that would be accurate.
Have you felt like yourself for at least a few weeks at any point since the accident?

Not really, no. I mean… I’ve had maybe a few better days where I could get through things and seem more normal, but I don’t think I’ve felt like myself for a few weeks straight.

It’s pretty much been going on since the retrofit accident, about a year and seven months ago. I wish I had a better answer than that.
Has anything significant changed in your life or environment since the accident, aside from your emotional state?

Yeah… I mean, some things have changed, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but at work I’ve had to hand off some of the floor responsibilities I used to handle myself.

And there was an interview with a regional director where I… didn’t handle myself well. I lost my composure and ended up walking out, which is embarrassing to say.

At home, things are different too. My marriage feels strained. I’m there, physically, but I’m not really participating the way I used to. Does that answer what you mean by changes?
Have there been any other significant stressors or changes in your life besides the accident and its aftermath?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean… life has its normal pressures, work and family and all that, but nothing I’d call a major new stressor separate from the accident and everything that followed.

I don’t want to overlook something, but… I think that’s the main thing. Does that answer it okay?
Have your symptoms been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years?

I’m not sure I can say two full years, no. It’s been… about a year and seven months since the retrofit accident, and that’s when this really started.

Most days since then, yeah, it’s been there in some form. But I don’t want to overstate it — it hasn’t been two years yet. Does that make sense?
Have your symptoms been present for at least two years?

No… not quite two years. It’s been going on since the retrofit accident, so about a year and seven months now. Most of it traces back to then, but I don’t want to say two years if that wouldn’t be accurate.
Have you felt consistently unwell or struggled with these feelings for the majority of the past year?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but for the majority of this past year, yes, I’ve been struggling with it.

It’s really been going on since the retrofit accident, about a year and seven months ago. So… yes, most of the past year would be accurate. Does that answer what you mean?
